claims.claim: Cameco spans multiple nuclear bottlenecks—tier-one uranium production, fuel services and Westinghouse exposure—linking reactor build/life-extension demand to scarce fuel-cycle and reactor-service capacity; increased Cigar Lake ownership deepens control of a high-quality upstream node.

factors.name: nuclear bottleneck control and substitution resilience
factors.basis: uranium production plus fuel services and Westinghouse participation diversify value capture across the nuclear chain rather than relying on one commodity layer

causalEdges.mechanism: operating and new reactors require secure fuel supply and long-lived technical services
causalEdges.falsifier: long-term contracting/pricing weakens persistently despite reactor growth

causalEdges.mechanism: scarce low-cost production supports contracting optionality in a constrained fuel market
causalEdges.falsifier: operational disruption or alternative supply materially erodes realized economics

risks.risk: Successor bottlenecks may sit in enrichment, conversion, construction labor or reactor delivery rather than uranium, limiting how much upstream scarcity translates into value capture.

unknowns.unknown: Exact future Westinghouse ownership/IPO economics and contract pricing mix remain unknown.

claims.claim: The structural nuclear thesis is not presently falsified, but quarter-level results demonstrate that mine disruptions, delivery timing and Westinghouse project variability can interrupt the path from favorable uranium fundamentals to reported earnings.

factors.name: operational concentration and timing risk
factors.basis: remote-mine performance and project timing can create earnings volatility even with strong long-term contracting conditions

causalEdges.from: remote asset disruption or delivery timing
causalEdges.mechanism: production and shipment timing can defer volumes/cash realization despite supportive long-term pricing
causalEdges.falsifier: diversified supply/inventory consistently absorbs disruptions without material earnings impact

risks.risk: Cigar Lake ownership concentration increases exposure to a high-quality asset but also magnifies site-specific operational risk.
Westinghouse adds project and execution exposure distinct from uranium-market fundamentals.

contradictions.claim: Supportive long-term nuclear/uranium fundamentals coexist with weaker quarter-level adjusted EBITDA and Westinghouse contribution.
contradictions.resolution: Treat as timing/execution variability rather than thesis falsification unless weakness persists across contracting and cash realization.

unknowns.unknown: No valuation or crowding conclusion is supported by the reused canonical evidence.
